# Handoff 01 - claude: framing panel A - measuring reviewers and workers (usage tiers, worker telemetry)

Date: 2026-10-14. Base commit: C3 `v0.2.1` (8a133f8); the PowerShell plugin `claude-codex-consult` 0.6.1 (main
dcb9d59, wave 30 unreleased). Both are the same program: a bridge that lets a coordinating agent (Claude Code, Codex
CLI and other hosts) consult reviewer models through their CLIs, with a reviewer roster, a findings store, and an
anonymised telemetry intake at `xelth.com/T/`. Read `README.md` and `docs/port/wave8-quota.md` of this repository
for the current behaviour; the roster shape is in the README's "Reviewer roster and panel".

## Question

Before any of this is implemented, we want the panel's angle on two measurement designs that will shape the
roster, the telemetry schema and the routing for a long time: (A) usage TIERS for the two standing consultants
(OpenAI gpt-6-astra through the ChatGPT subscription, Zhipu glm-5.3 through z.ai) - which reasoning effort to
send for which purpose, and how to score a tier; (B) WORKER telemetry - the coordinator's own sub-agents (Claude
Code tiers haiku / sonnet / opus / fable AND their effort levels) counted and scored at near-zero token cost so the
tier choice can be improved from data. Both change a closed telemetry vocabulary that is hard to change once
published.

## Task state

- Done: the telemetry intake (consult and rating events; engine, vendor class, a closed list of model names, purpose,
  outcome class, counts - never a task, prompt, path or name); the quota windows (wave 8: the 5-hour and weekly
  ChatGPT windows read from the Codex rollouts; a round of review costs 8-23 % of the 5-hour window at effort high;
  a forked thread with sub-agents once cost 96 % in 186 s); effort vocabularies per endpoint (caps-v1: openai
  low|medium|high|xhigh; z.ai low|high|max with medium->high and xhigh->max); purpose presets (chore low, checkpoint
  medium, acceptance high, core-contract/stuck xhigh); the ratings (`rate`, `useful yes|partly|no`) per
  consultation; a routed panel seats reviewers by track record.
- Open: no telemetry event carries the effort; no event exists for workers at all; the roster has no per-purpose
  effort policy per entry; nothing measures a tier against its cost.
- Not in scope: new reviewer engines; the browser engine; the intake's hosting.

## Evidence

- `crates/c3/src/telemetry/classes.rs` - the closed vocabulary of the events (what can be added without breaking
  the published schema).
- `crates/c3-core/src/quota.rs` - what a run costs in window share and tokens (`tokens`, `quota`, `budget` in the
  ledger entry): the cost side of a score exists per consultation already.
- `.collab/parity-0.6.1-2026-10-08/state.md`, sections "Planned (2026-10-14 10:40): usage tiers" and "Planned
  after the tag: worker telemetry" - the coordinator's current sketch (below).
- Observed today: nine review rounds of one wave with gpt-6-astra at effort high found one real defect each
  (F46-1 .. F62-1), 183-234 s and 10-15 % of the 5-hour window per round; a GLM round at `max` is cheaper in money
  and has no 5-hour window; Claude Code workers (opus / sonnet) did each fix in 15-70 minutes.

## The coordinator's sketch (to be challenged)

(A) Usage tiers. Roster entries get an effort POLICY per purpose (e.g. gpt-6-astra: chore medium, reading pass
medium, diff-review high, core-contract xhigh; glm-5.3: chore low, review high, stuck max). The consult and
rating events carry `effort` (the tier SENT after the vocabulary mapping - closed: none|low|medium|high|xhigh|max)
and `effort_requested` (the preset name). The intake's usefulness table splits per reviewer x effort. Routing
"scout and judge": a cheap tier (GLM low, or a Haiku worker) reads the diff and writes a digest handoff; the judge
(Astra high, or GLM max) gets the digest plus a call cap; the digest survives a cold cache. Open: does z.ai expose
more than three tiers on glm-5.3; is `medium` on gpt-6-astra good enough for a reading pass; how to SCORE a tier -
usefulness per 5-hour-window share, not per run.

(B) Worker telemetry. Claude Code's `SubagentStop` hook (the plugin can ship it) fires at each worker's end with
the agent type; the bridge records one closed-class event per worker: tier (haiku|sonnet|opus|fable|other), effort
level if the host exposes it, duration class, outcome class (reported | stopped-by-coordinator | error | unknown),
and a coordinator-side mark after the fact (`c3 workers rate <id> useful yes|partly|no`) - never the brief, the
files or the repository. The intake gets a "workers" table (counts, error share, usefulness per tier x effort).
Cost: one hook invocation per worker, no model tokens. Open: can the hook see the effort and the tier reliably
(agent definition vs model alias); how to attribute a wave's success to a worker when the coordinator reworked it;
what a user of another host (Codex CLI agents, Kimi) can report.

## Alternatives weighed

1. **Effort policy in the roster + effort in the events (the sketch)** - small schema change now; the score needs
   months of data.
2. **No new telemetry; a local experiment first** (the coordinator runs the same brief at two efforts for a week and
   compares findings per window share) - no schema risk; nothing learned for other users.
3. **Score reviewers by findings confirmed, not by usefulness marks** - more objective (a finding later marked
   `implemented`/`verified` is a hit); needs the findings store joined to the events (ids are private today).
4. **Workers: no hook, the coordinator's own notes in STATE.md** - zero code; not comparable across users.

Current preference: 1 for reviewers with the window-share denominator; 3 as the long-term score once the findings
join exists; for workers the hook with closed classes, but only if the effort is visible to it.

## Questions

- **Q1.** For (A): which effort tiers would you send per purpose for gpt-6-astra and glm-5.3, and what is the right
  denominator to score a tier (window share, money, wall time, findings confirmed)? Name a design we did not list.
- **Q2.** For (B): is the SubagentStop hook the right capture point; what MUST stay out of the event for privacy;
  and how would you attribute a worker's result when the coordinator reworks it?
- **Q3.** The schema: which fields would you add to the closed vocabulary now so we never have to break it later?
- **Q4.** The "scout and judge" routing: where does it fail (a digest that hides the defect), and what cap on the
  scout's output keeps the judge honest?

Answer by number. Keep it under 600 words.

## 8b - the equal-time tie (reviewer finding F46-1)

`endpoint_window` took a candidate only when its `observed_at` was STRICTLY newer, so at an equal
timestamp (the ledger writes `observed_at` without fractional seconds, ties are likely) the first
entry stayed: a 30 % observation could hide a 99 % one and the reviewer stayed available. The
recorded-observation selection and the live-rollout replacement now share ONE comparison
(`quota::window_obs_wins`): newer `observed_at` wins; at an equal instant the higher primary
`used_percent` wins, then the higher secondary (the rule `newer_wins` already applied to rollouts).
Tests: `endpoint_window_at_an_equal_time_keeps_the_fuller_window_in_both_orders` and
`the_live_window_replaces_a_lower_recorded_one_at_an_equal_time` (both failed before the fix).
`observed_at` comparison sites: `quota.rs` recorded selection (fixed), live replacement (fixed),
`newer_wins` (already correct); `health.rs` only consumes `endpoint_window` (n.a.); the machine-wide
record merge has no `observed_at` comparison (n.a.).

Plugin parity: `codex-consult-common.ps1` `Get-EndpointWindow` (lines ~6985 and ~6989) uses
`-gt $best.ObservedAt` for both the recorded and the live selection - the SAME tie. A plugin
TECH_DEBT candidate (not edited here).

## 8c - the equal-time merge per window (reviewer finding F48-1)

The 8b tuple rule (primary first) could hide a blocking weekly window: at an equal `observed_at`,
primary 40 % / secondary 99 % lost to primary 50 % / secondary 20 %. The coordinator's rule: at an
EQUAL `observed_at` the windows merge PER WINDOW - the endpoint's primary is the observation with
the higher primary `used_percent` (with that observation's reset), the secondary independently the
higher secondary (with its reset); a strictly newer `observed_at` still replaces both.
`quota::select_window` (recorded and live selection of `endpoint_window`, replacing
`window_obs_wins`) and `quota::merge_observation` (the sub-agent and account-rollout aggregation,
built on `newer_wins`, which still decides newer-or-not) apply it. Tests:
`endpoint_window_at_an_equal_time_merges_per_window_in_both_orders`,
`the_live_window_merges_per_window_with_a_crossing_recorded_one` (both assignments),
`merge_observation_keeps_each_fuller_window_at_an_equal_instant`; the 8b tests stay.
The plugin's T17 fix of the tie (see 8b) must use the same per-window rule.

## 8d - a total order for tied windows (reviewer finding F50-1)

At an equal `observed_at` and an equal `used_percent` the per-window pick kept the FIRST window's
reset, so a null or past reset could hide a future one by ordering. One comparator
(`quota::cmp_window_rank`, used by `select_window` for the recorded and live selections and by
`merge_observation`) now ranks two observations of the same window at the comparison time `now`:
(1) a known FUTURE reset beats a known PAST reset beats a missing (null) one; (2) the higher
`used_percent`; (3) the later `resets_at`; (4) identical - either. A strictly newer `observed_at`
still replaces both windows. Tests: `equal_shares_rank_by_the_reset_in_every_order`,
`the_live_window_ranks_a_future_reset_over_a_null_one_at_a_tie`,
`a_past_reset_never_hides_a_future_one_whatever_the_share`,
`the_tie_selection_is_the_same_for_every_permutation` (4 observations, all 24 orders).
The plugin's T17 fix must use this full ordering (future > past > null, then share, then later reset).

## 8e - one comparison instant, finite percentages (reviewer findings F52-1, F52-2)

The 8d rank depends on `now`, and each comparison sampled the clock on its own, so a reset crossing
from future to past DURING one aggregation (the rollout reads happen between merges) made the pick
order-dependent (A=(100 %, R), B=(99 %, S), C=(30 %, S), R < S). `now` is now sampled ONCE at the
top of each public entry point - `endpoint_window` (-> `endpoint_window_at`), `account_window`
(-> `account_window_at`), `codex_run_quota` - and passed as a parameter to `select_window`,
`merge_observation` and `cmp_window_rank` (no clock read inside the comparator); the health
evaluation hands the same `now_utc` to `endpoint_window_at` and to the "reset in the past" verdict.
F52-2: `finite_percent` treats a non-finite or out-of-range (outside 0..=100) share - a "NaN" /
"inf" text included - as an ABSENT window, in the window states (the block evaluation), the
selection and the rollout parser; the comparator uses `f64::total_cmp`. Tests:
`one_comparison_instant_makes_the_aggregation_order_independent` (A/B/C, all 6 orders, an instant
before R keeps A, one between R and S keeps B, both block),
`a_non_finite_percent_never_hides_a_valid_block`,
`the_tie_selection_is_the_same_for_every_order_of_six` (720 orders, a past reset and a NaN included).
The plugin's T17 fix needs the same single instant and the finite check.

## 8f - the account cache keeps raw observations, newer invalid windows do not replace (F55-1, F55-2)

F55-1: `account_window` cached only the WINNER picked at an earlier instant and returned it for 60 s,
so after that winner's reset a discarded equal-time observation that still blocked was lost. The
cache (per codex home) now holds the RAW observations of the account's rollouts
(`read_account_observations`); `account_window_at` runs the selection (`merge_observation`) at
every lookup with the requested `now`, the 60 s TTL only bounds how often the rollouts are read.
F55-2 (fail closed, per window): an observation with no VALID window is absent; a strictly newer
observation replaces a window only where its own window is valid, otherwise the older valid window
of that kind stays, and an older observation fills only the kinds the newer one lacks - in
`select_window` (recorded and live) and in `merge_observation`; at an equal instant the 8d rank
decides. Tests: `the_account_cache_selects_at_each_requested_instant`,
`a_newer_invalid_record_keeps_the_older_valid_window` (NaN / out of range, both orders, plus the
newer-partial case), and the permutation test now runs 5040 orders of seven observations (a
NaN-only newer record included). The tests that read `endpoint_window` are serialised with those
that switch the process-wide live source on (a flake of the shared global). The plugin's T17 fix
needs the same cache shape and the per-window validation.

## 8g - every window carries its OWN observation instant (reviewer finding F58-1)

Partial-window aggregation kept an older observation's window but stamped the aggregate with the
NEWER observation's instant, so a later comparison treated the retained window as newer than it
was: with t1 < t2 < t3, A = primary 30 % at t1, B = secondary 10 % at t3, C = primary 99 % at t2,
the fold A, B, C kept 30 % (B had promoted A's primary to t3) and A, C, B kept 99 %. Now
`Observation` carries `primary_at` / `secondary_at` (`window_at(kind)`: its own, else `at`),
`EndpointWindow` and `AccountWindow` carry `window_at: [primary, secondary]`, and a candidate window
is compared only with the instant of THAT retained window (strictly newer replaces, equal takes the
8d rank, older is kept; an invalid window has no instant and never replaces). The aggregate
`observed_at` / `at` is derived (the latest per-window instant) for display and the age of the
record, never for a replacement decision. The instants flow: rollout parse (`at` of the event) ->
`merge_observation` (per-window instants kept) -> `account_window_at` (`AccountWindow.window_at`
from the aggregate, over the raw cache) -> `endpoint_window_at` (recorded candidates carry their
entry instant on both windows, the live candidate its `window_at`) -> `select_window` (compares per
window with `EndpointWindow.window_at`). Tests: `partial_windows_keep_their_own_instants_in_the_recorded_selection`,
`partial_windows_keep_their_own_instants_in_merge_observation`,
`partial_windows_keep_their_own_instants_across_the_recorded_live_split`,
`distinct_instant_partial_windows_are_order_independent` (720 orders, distinct instants, partial
windows, a NaN-only one). The plugin's T17 fix needs per-window timestamps too.

## 8h - the per-window instants survive persistence (reviewer finding F60-1, supersedes F58-1)

8g kept each window's instant in memory, but `Observation::to_quota` wrote ONE aggregate
`observed_at`, so a recorded aggregate (the ledger's `quota`, the machine-wide health record - both
carry the quota object verbatim) lost the provenance: `endpoint_window_at` rebuilt both instants
from it, and an aggregate of A (primary 30 at t1) and B (secondary 10 at t3) labelled its primary
with t3 and beat C (primary 99 at t2). The quota record now carries two optional keys after
`observed_at`: `primary_observed_at` and `secondary_observed_at` (ISO, local offset), written by
`to_quota` only for a window that is present (a null quota keeps exactly `primary, secondary,
observed_at`). They are written wherever the quota is written (the ledger entry of a codex run, the
machine-wide record) and read by the recorded selection in `endpoint_window_at`; the aggregate
`observed_at` is only the LEGACY fallback of a record written before 8h (keys absent), and the
selected `EndpointWindow.quota` is re-stamped with them. Plugin compatibility: the oracle reads
only keys it knows; its one strict key check is on the NULL quota (`primary,secondary,observed_at`),
which is unchanged. Tests: `the_quota_record_carries_per_window_instants_through_ledger_and_health`,
`a_persisted_aggregate_cannot_promote_its_older_window` (both recorded orders and C live),
`a_legacy_record_without_window_instants_uses_the_aggregate_instant`. The plugin's T17 fix needs
the same two ledger fields.

## 8i - lossless instants, the imprecise rule, the legacy policy (reviewer finding F62-1)

8h stored each window's instant through a seconds-only formatter, so a recorded 99 % observed at
12:00:00.900 read back as 12:00:00 and an OLDER live 30 % at 12:00:00.100 looked strictly newer and
replaced it. Three rules now:
1. **Lossless**: `primary_observed_at` / `secondary_observed_at` are written as RFC3339 with the
   fractional seconds the instant has (`2026-10-13T12:00:00.900+00:00`; no fraction when it has none),
   in `to_quota` and in the re-stamp of `select_window`; read back exactly. The aggregate
   `observed_at` keeps its seconds-only format (compat).
2. **Imprecise compare** (`cmp_instants`): an instant without a fractional part is imprecise (a legacy
   aggregate, a second-precision record, a whole-second rollout stamp). If either side is, the two
   are compared at whole-second granularity: a recency win needs a strictly later whole second, the
   same second is a tie and the 8d rank decides (future reset > past > null, higher share, later
   reset). Both precise: exact. (A precise instant that happens to be exactly on a second reads as
   imprecise - the conservative side.)
3. **Legacy records** (no per-window keys): the window instants are UNKNOWN (`EndpointWindow.
   window_legacy`; the aggregate stands in only for the legacy-vs-legacy comparison). A legacy window
   never wins on recency against a window with a known instant - that pair is decided by the 8d rank
   alone; no per-window key is written for a legacy window.
Tests: `a_subsecond_instant_survives_the_record_and_beats_an_older_live_one`,
`a_second_precision_record_ties_with_a_live_instant_of_the_same_second`,
`a_legacy_record_never_wins_on_recency_against_a_known_instant` (replaces the 8h legacy test; the
health verdict sees the block). Pairwise comparisons mixing precise and imprecise instants are not
strictly transitive across three or more observations within one second; the rank keeps each pair
deterministic. The plugin's T17 fix needs the same three rules.

## 8j - ONE total order per window (supersedes the 8i pairwise precision rule)

The 8i rule (whole-second compare only when a side is imprecise) was not transitive across mixed
precisions inside one second, and a legacy window decided by rank against known ones broke the fold
the same way. Now every instant comparison in the selection and the merge is made at WHOLE-SECOND
granularity (`cmp_instants`: floor to the second; fractions are never an ordering key): a strictly
later second wins on recency; the same second is a tie that `cmp_window_rank` (8d) decides. The
fractional instants stay stored, re-stamped and round-tripped exactly (8i) - bookkeeping, not a
key. Within one kind of window (known instants, or legacy aggregates compared at the same
granularity) (floor second, rank) is a lexicographic total order. The legacy rule stays - an unknown
instant never wins on recency against a known one, the rank alone decides - and to keep the fold
order-independent `select_window` keeps the best KNOWN and the best LEGACY candidate per window
(`EndpointWindow` slots) and resolves the visible window from that pair (the legacy one only if it
outranks the known one by the rank), so the pick is a function of the candidate SET. Inside one
second the higher-usage window wins: the conservative side (usage only rises within a window; a
reset is already ranked by future/past). Tests: `whole_second_order_is_transitive_for_the_abc_precision_case`
(a imprecise :00 50 %, b :00.100 99 %, c :00.900 30 %, six orders -> 99 %),
`mixed_precision_candidates_give_one_pick_in_every_order` (six candidates - two imprecise, two with
fractions in one second, one in the next second, one legacy, partial windows - 720 orders through
the recorded selection and `merge_observation`, plus a recorded/live split); the 8i sub-second test
now passes by rank (99 % at :00.900 against live 30 % at :00.100). The plugin's T17 fix uses the
same total order.

## What it is

A coordinator â€” your Claude Code, Codex CLI or any shell session â€” asks a **roster of
reviewers from different labs** to look at a one-page brief. Reviewers are read-only:
nothing is edited by them. Every consultation is recorded as files next to the code (the
brief, the reviewer's reply verbatim, a JSON ledger, **findings tracked by id** that you
verify and move yourself), and a **panel** runs several reviewers in parallel and
reconciles them. Reviewers are subscriptions the user already has: the ChatGPT plan through
the Codex CLI, z.ai GLM, Xiaomi MiMo or any Responses-API provider through a
`[model_providers.<name>]` table, Gemini through Google's Antigravity CLI `agy`, Meta Muse
through the Muse Code CLI, Claude through Claude Code headless (`claude -p`; the subscription,
an API key, or a coding plan's Anthropic-compatible endpoint). The bridge never creates, prints,
stores or commits a key. C3 adds
one API path for people who will not juggle subscriptions - OpenRouter (or any
OpenAI-compatible endpoint) through a native `http` engine that reads its key from the
environment and sends the reviewer a prepared pack instead of tools - and, on top of the
same files, packs for chat models, a local SurrealDB index and telemetry-driven panel
routing. The design is in [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md).

One static binary instead of PowerShell 5.1/7 on three OSes; a typed ledger and findings
store; the same behaviour under Claude Code, Codex CLI and a plain shell without a host
adapter (plugin ROADMAP R13, host invariance); and a place to make the bridge fast enough
to run a panel non-blocking (R12).

## Quota windows and the reading budget (plugin wave 30; C3 wave 8)

A subscription's quota is spent in windows - on a ChatGPT plan a 5-hour window and a weekly one -
and ONE review can spend a whole 5-hour window: a fork replays its parent's context on every tool
call, and a reviewer's own sub-agents replay theirs. C3 reads what Codex itself writes into each
thread's rollout (`<codex home>/sessions/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/rollout-<ts>-<thread>.jsonl`, the last
`token_count` that names a window) and acts on it, as the plugin does (`docs/port/wave8-quota.md`):

- **Ledger** (codex runs, after `commit_wait_ms`): `quota {primary, secondary, observed_at}`,
  `tokens {input, cached, output, thread_input, calls, max_input, context_window, subagents {count,
  input, calls}}` (the run's share of the thread's running total - a fork inherits its parent's),
  `subagents_allowed`, `budget`; the summary's `quota      :` line and the handoff's
  `Quota (rollout):` line.
- **Verdict**: the newest observed window of an endpoint (its ledgers, the machine-wide health
  records - which now carry `quota` - and, for the built-in `openai` endpoint while the
  machine-wide health is on, the codex home's newest rollout): at 98 % or more with its reset ahead
  the endpoint is `unavailable (5-hour window 99 % used, resets <iso>)` like a usage limit with a
  known reset (roster walk, `--require`, panel, `--short`, a real run refused); at 80 % or more the
  verdict says `available (low quota: 5-hour window 84 % until 18:32)`. `c3 providers` has a QUOTA
  column (`5h 96% until 18:32; wk 15% until Oct 20`) and `--json` rows a `quota` object.
- **`--budget <percent>`** (env `CODEX_CONSULT_QUOTA_BUDGET`, default 90, 0 = off): the stall watch
  reads the run's rollout every 15 s and stops the main turn at the budget - the partial kept, no
  continuation, `failed: stopped at the quota budget: 5-hour window 91 % used, resets 18:32; the
  partial is kept` (provider_failure class `operator`, telemetry class `quota`).
- **Replay guard**: a `--mode fork|resume` whose parent rollout is over `CODEX_CONSULT_FORK_MAX_KB`
  (default 512) is refused before anything starts; from 128 KB on it is warned about.
- **Sub-agents off**: every codex turn passes `-c features.multi_agent=false` right after `-m`
  unless `--codex-config` (or the roster's `codex_config`) names `features.multi_agent`.
- **Reading discipline**: the purpose paragraphs of acceptance, diff-review, checkpoint and
  core-contract end with the plugin's block (`git diff <range> --stat` first, one path at a time
  with a line cap, the documents first, the verdict even on an incomplete read).

## Telemetry (on by default, off with one line)

Installing C3 means accepting these terms. C3 reports **one anonymous event per
consultation** (and one per usefulness rating) to the maintainer's intake,
<https://xelth.com/T/>, so the bridge can be improved when someone the maintainer never hears
from uses it. Everything collected is shown in the open, as counts, on <https://xelth.com/C3/>.

* **Sent - classes only:** `app_id` (`c3`), the C3 version, an instance id
  (`sha256(salt file + machine name)` â€” stable per installation, meaningless elsewhere), a
  severity, and `details`: the engine, the reviewer's VENDOR CLASS and model (below), the purpose
  (one of the eight purposes, `none` or `other`), the outcome class (`usable`,
  `usable-after-continuation`, `failed:<class>` with a closed class), wall seconds, token counts,
  findings counts, structured or not, a format retry or not, panel size, the federation peer
  COUNT, OS, runtime, and `consult_ref` (below). `tags` repeat `[provider, model]`.
* **The rating event** (`c3 findings --rate`, `c3 telemetry --backfill-ratings`): `details` exactly
  `engine, provider, model, purpose, mark, age_days, bridge_version, os, ps_version, judge,
  rating_rev, consult_ref` (the plugin's 0.6.1 shape; `ps_version` is `unknown` - C3 runs no
  PowerShell), `title` the mark, `client_time` the MARK's own time on every path. `judge` is
  `{provider, model, source}` - who gave the mark, resolved at rating time and saved in the mark:
  `rating_actor` (`CODEX_CONSULT_COORDINATOR` of the rating process), `consult_coordinator` (the
  coordinator the consultation recorded) or `unknown` - classes only, never a label or a host.
  `rating_rev` is the mark's revision (1 + the consultation's highest); the intake keeps per
  `(instance_id, consult_ref)` the rating with the highest `rating_rev`.
* **`consult_ref`:** a random id minted for each consultation (a lower-case guid, derived from
  nothing - not the `consult_id` the reviewer sees), kept in the ledger right after `consult_id`
  and sent in the consultation event and every rating event of it, so the intake can link them.
  A pseudonymous correlation key: whoever holds both the telemetry and a shared `sessions.json`
  can join them on it.
* **The classes** (the plugin's closed vendor table; `c3/src/telemetry/classes.rs`): the vendor
  class is derived from the HOST of the endpoint the reviewer talked to (`openai` - also Codex's
  built-in provider -, `zai`, `xiaomi`, `byteplus`, `moonshot`, `alibaba`, `minimax`), else from
  the engine (`agy` google, `muse` meta, `claude` anthropic), else `other`; the model is sent only
  when it EQUALS an entry of that class's closed list (after lower-casing, `[1m]` stripped),
  else `other` (`unknown` without a model). A roster label, a model or a purpose as typed - say
  `customer-acme` - never leaves the machine. **C3 extension (the `http` engine):** the host
  `openrouter.ai` is the class `openrouter`; its model is sent in OpenRouter's `<vendor>/<model>`
  form only when the vendor slug is one of `openai`, `anthropic`, `google`, `z-ai`, `moonshotai`,
  `minimax`, `xiaomi`, `qwen` (alibaba's list), `meta-llama` (meta's list) AND the model part
  equals an entry of that class's list (`openai/gpt-5.1`), else `other`; an http endpoint of a
  listed vendor's host takes that vendor's class, any other host `other`.
* **Never:** task names, prompts, briefs, paths, thread ids, `consult_id`, finding texts, notes,
  topics, labels as typed, the coordinator's host, user names, keys. The server drops
  secret-named keys on arrival and reports how many; C3 treats a non-zero count as its own bug.
* **Off:** `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY=off` (any value other than unset/`on`/`1`/`true`/`yes`
  counts as off), or `--telemetry off` per run - a run's own `--telemetry on|off` wins over the
  variable, and a panel passes it to its members. The first run after an install prints this
  notice once; the dry run says whether it is on.
* **Never blocks a run; never lost silently:** events queue in C3's own outbox
  (`<codex home>/c3/telemetry/spool.ndjson`, one `{v, kind, queued_unix, body}` line each - not
  the plugin's `telemetry-spool/`: C3 is its own app with its own salt and instance id), are sent
  by a detached sender a run starts right after its commit (a consultation, a panel - once -, a
  rating, a backfill; the run never waits for it, and it gets an allow-listed environment only: no
  key, no host marker) in batches of at most 100 (one flush ends after 60 s, one request after 8 s),
  retried by the next sender and dropped 7 days after they were queued. The sender follows the
  intake's answers as the plugin does: a 429 whose `Retry-After` is at most 60 s is waited for
  once (else the batch stays queued), a 400 naming `events[i]` drops that event and resends the
  rest (at most three per flush), a 413 halves the batch and drops an event too large alone -
  each refused event is one line of the last flush's `rejected` - and a 403, another refusal or no
  answer stops the flush with the outbox kept. Appends and the sender are synchronised by a lock,
  and the sender removes only the lines it delivered or dropped - an event queued while it sends
  stays queued. The sender lock's owner record (`flush.owner.json`) lets `--status` and a refused
  sender say "sender busy since <t>", and after 30 minutes "sender stuck since <t> (pid <n>)". An event that cannot be
  spooled is said and counted (`c3 telemetry --status`); a rating's event is retried and else
  left for `c3 telemetry --backfill-ratings`.
* **Complaints:** `c3 --complain "<text>"` prints the exact payload (your text plus the last
  ledger entry's summary - classes only), asks before sending, and prints a public reference
  like `T-7KQ4-M2XZ` to quote on the forum section <https://xelth.com/F/p/c3> or in a mail.
* **Delete my data:** `c3 forget-me` (or `c3 telemetry --forget --public-ref <ref> [--local]`,
  or `DELETE https://xelth.com/T/v2/instances/<instance_id>?public_ref=<ref>`) asks the intake to
  remove every event and complaint this installation ever sent - proved by a complaint's public
  reference - and removes the local salt, outbox and references only AFTER the intake confirmed
  it. A DELETE the intake does not confirm deletes nothing locally: the instance id and the
  reference stay, the pending deletion is recorded (`forget-pending.json`) and nothing is
  spooled or sent until `c3 forget-me` retries it with the same identity and the intake
  confirms. Without any public reference the intake cannot verify ownership:
  `c3 forget-me --local` (or `c3 telemetry --forget --local`) removes the local data only, and
  says that the intake keeps what was sent.
* **`c3 telemetry`:** `--status` (the switch and its source, the intake, the outbox, the events
  not spooled since the last flush, the sender lock's owner, a pending deletion, the last flush,
  the instance id),
  `--flush`, `--forget`, `--backfill-ratings [--dry-run]`. The intake is
  `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY_URL` when set (https only; plain http only to a loopback host in test
  mode), else `https://xelth.com/T`.

Windows 11 is where every harness ran and where the PowerShell plugin's evals are the oracle;

Linux: process liveness and the tree kill come from `/proc` and `kill` instead of the Win32
APIs and `taskkill /T`, the file locks are `flock` advisory locks instead of share modes, and
a detached run is a child in its own process group instead of a `cmd.exe` launch; the files
written are the same bytes. The tests that need Windows (cmd.exe launchers, Windows launcher
paths) are gated `#[cfg(windows)]` with a reason each. macOS is untested. For a sandbox whose

`HTTPS_PROXY`, `C3_HTTP_AUTH_PROXY=<host,...>` (no `Authorization` header, no key read) and
`C3_HTTP_CA_BUNDLE=<pem>` (extra trust anchors) â€” see `docs/port/linux-port.md`.

`crates/c3` (runtime modules), `crates/c3-cli` (the binary). Each ported piece brings its

108: higher secondary (with its reset); a strictly newer `observed_at` still replaces both.
109: `quota::select_window` (recorded and live selection of `endpoint_window`, replacing

117: ## 8d - a total order for tied windows (reviewer finding F50-1)

120: reset, so a null or past reset could hide a future one by ordering. One comparator
121: (`quota::cmp_window_rank`, used by `select_window` for the recorded and live selections and by
122: `merge_observation`) now ranks two observations of the same window at the comparison time `now`:
123: (1) a known FUTURE reset beats a known PAST reset beats a missing (null) one; (2) the higher
124: `used_percent`; (3) the later `resets_at`; (4) identical - either. A strictly newer `observed_at`
125: still replaces both windows. Tests: `equal_shares_rank_by_the_reset_in_every_order`,
126: `the_live_window_ranks_a_future_reset_over_a_null_one_at_a_tie`,
127: `a_past_reset_never_hides_a_future_one_whatever_the_share`,
128: `the_tie_selection_is_the_same_for_every_permutation` (4 observations, all 24 orders).

131: ## 8e - one comparison instant, finite percentages (reviewer findings F52-1, F52-2)
132: 
133: The 8d rank depends on `now`, and each comparison sampled the clock on its own, so a reset crossing
134: from future to past DURING one aggregation (the rollout reads happen between merges) made the pick
135: order-dependent (A=(100 %, R), B=(99 %, S), C=(30 %, S), R < S). `now` is now sampled ONCE at the
136: top of each public entry point - `endpoint_window` (-> `endpoint_window_at`), `account_window`
137: (-> `account_window_at`), `codex_run_quota` - and passed as a parameter to `select_window`,
138: `merge_observation` and `cmp_window_rank` (no clock read inside the comparator); the health
139: evaluation hands the same `now_utc` to `endpoint_window_at` and to the "reset in the past" verdict.
140: F52-2: `finite_percent` treats a non-finite or out-of-range (outside 0..=100) share - a "NaN" /
141: "inf" text included - as an ABSENT window, in the window states (the block evaluation), the
142: selection and the rollout parser; the comparator uses `f64::total_cmp`. Tests:
143: `one_comparison_instant_makes_the_aggregation_order_independent` (A/B/C, all 6 orders, an instant
144: before R keeps A, one between R and S keeps B, both block),
145: `a_non_finite_percent_never_hides_a_valid_block`,
146: `the_tie_selection_is_the_same_for_every_order_of_six` (720 orders, a past reset and a NaN included).

149: ## 8f - the account cache keeps raw observations, newer invalid windows do not replace (F55-1, F55-2)
150: 
151: F55-1: `account_window` cached only the WINNER picked at an earlier instant and returned it for 60 s,
152: so after that winner's reset a discarded equal-time observation that still blocked was lost. The
153: cache (per codex home) now holds the RAW observations of the account's rollouts
154: (`read_account_observations`); `account_window_at` runs the selection (`merge_observation`) at
155: every lookup with the requested `now`, the 60 s TTL only bounds how often the rollouts are read.
156: F55-2 (fail closed, per window): an observation with no VALID window is absent; a strictly newer
157: observation replaces a window only where its own window is valid, otherwise the older valid window
158: of that kind stays, and an older observation fills only the kinds the newer one lacks - in
159: `select_window` (recorded and live) and in `merge_observation`; at an equal instant the 8d rank

161: `a_newer_invalid_record_keeps_the_older_valid_window` (NaN / out of range, both orders, plus the

163: NaN-only newer record included). The tests that read `endpoint_window` are serialised with those

165: needs the same cache shape and the per-window validation.

167: ## 8g - every window carries its OWN observation instant (reviewer finding F58-1)
168: 
169: Partial-window aggregation kept an older observation's window but stamped the aggregate with the
170: NEWER observation's instant, so a later comparison treated the retained window as newer than it
171: was: with t1 < t2 < t3, A = primary 30 % at t1, B = secondary 10 % at t3, C = primary 99 % at t2,
172: the fold A, B, C kept 30 % (B had promoted A's primary to t3) and A, C, B kept 99 %. Now
173: `Observation` carries `primary_at` / `secondary_at` (`window_at(kind)`: its own, else `at`),
174: `EndpointWindow` and `AccountWindow` carry `window_at: [primary, secondary]`, and a candidate window
175: is compared only with the instant of THAT retained window (strictly newer replaces, equal takes the
176: 8d rank, older is kept; an invalid window has no instant and never replaces). The aggregate
177: `observed_at` / `at` is derived (the latest per-window instant) for display and the age of the
178: record, never for a replacement decision. The instants flow: rollout parse (`at` of the event) ->
179: `merge_observation` (per-window instants kept) -> `account_window_at` (`AccountWindow.window_at`
180: from the aggregate, over the raw cache) -> `endpoint_window_at` (recorded candidates carry their
181: entry instant on both windows, the live candidate its `window_at`) -> `select_window` (compares per
182: window with `EndpointWindow.window_at`). Tests: `partial_windows_keep_their_own_instants_in_the_recorded_selection`,
183: `partial_windows_keep_their_own_instants_in_merge_observation`,
184: `partial_windows_keep_their_own_instants_across_the_recorded_live_split`,
185: `distinct_instant_partial_windows_are_order_independent` (720 orders, distinct instants, partial
186: windows, a NaN-only one). The plugin's T17 fix needs per-window timestamps too.
187: 
188: ## 8h - the per-window instants survive persistence (reviewer finding F60-1, supersedes F58-1)
189: 
190: 8g kept each window's instant in memory, but `Observation::to_quota` wrote ONE aggregate
191: `observed_at`, so a recorded aggregate (the ledger's `quota`, the machine-wide health record - both
192: carry the quota object verbatim) lost the provenance: `endpoint_window_at` rebuilt both instants
193: from it, and an aggregate of A (primary 30 at t1) and B (secondary 10 at t3) labelled its primary
194: with t3 and beat C (primary 99 at t2). The quota record now carries two optional keys after
195: `observed_at`: `primary_observed_at` and `secondary_observed_at` (ISO, local offset), written by
196: `to_quota` only for a window that is present (a null quota keeps exactly `primary, secondary,
197: observed_at`). They are written wherever the quota is written (the ledger entry of a codex run, the
198: machine-wide record) and read by the recorded selection in `endpoint_window_at`; the aggregate
199: `observed_at` is only the LEGACY fallback of a record written before 8h (keys absent), and the
200: selected `EndpointWindow.quota` is re-stamped with them. Plugin compatibility: the oracle reads
201: only keys it knows; its one strict key check is on the NULL quota (`primary,secondary,observed_at`),
202: which is unchanged. Tests: `the_quota_record_carries_per_window_instants_through_ledger_and_health`,
203: `a_persisted_aggregate_cannot_promote_its_older_window` (both recorded orders and C live),
204: `a_legacy_record_without_window_instants_uses_the_aggregate_instant`. The plugin's T17 fix needs
205: the same two ledger fields.
206: 
207: ## 8i - lossless instants, the imprecise rule, the legacy policy (reviewer finding F62-1)
208: 
209: 8h stored each window's instant through a seconds-only formatter, so a recorded 99 % observed at
210: 12:00:00.900 read back as 12:00:00 and an OLDER live 30 % at 12:00:00.100 looked strictly newer and
211: replaced it. Three rules now:
212: 1. **Lossless**: `primary_observed_at` / `secondary_observed_at` are written as RFC3339 with the
213:    fractional seconds the instant has (`2026-10-13T12:00:00.900+00:00`; no fraction when it has none),
214:    in `to_quota` and in the re-stamp of `select_window`; read back exactly. The aggregate
215:    `observed_at` keeps its seconds-only format (compat).
216: 2. **Imprecise compare** (`cmp_instants`): an instant without a fractional part is imprecise (a legacy
217:    aggregate, a second-precision record, a whole-second rollout stamp). If either side is, the two
218:    are compared at whole-second granularity: a recency win needs a strictly later whole second, the
219:    same second is a tie and the 8d rank decides (future reset > past > null, higher share, later
220:    reset). Both precise: exact. (A precise instant that happens to be exactly on a second reads as
221:    imprecise - the conservative side.)
222: 3. **Legacy records** (no per-window keys): the window instants are UNKNOWN (`EndpointWindow.
223:    window_legacy`; the aggregate stands in only for the legacy-vs-legacy comparison). A legacy window
224:    never wins on recency against a window with a known instant - that pair is decided by the 8d rank
225:    alone; no per-window key is written for a legacy window.
226: Tests: `a_subsecond_instant_survives_the_record_and_beats_an_older_live_one`,
227: `a_second_precision_record_ties_with_a_live_instant_of_the_same_second`,
228: `a_legacy_record_never_wins_on_recency_against_a_known_instant` (replaces the 8h legacy test; the
229: health verdict sees the block). Pairwise comparisons mixing precise and imprecise instants are not
230: strictly transitive across three or more observations within one second; the rank keeps each pair
231: deterministic. The plugin's T17 fix needs the same three rules.
232: 
233: ## 8j - ONE total order per window (supersedes the 8i pairwise precision rule)
234: 
235: The 8i rule (whole-second compare only when a side is imprecise) was not transitive across mixed
236: precisions inside one second, and a legacy window decided by rank against known ones broke the fold
237: the same way. Now every instant comparison in the selection and the merge is made at WHOLE-SECOND
238: granularity (`cmp_instants`: floor to the second; fractions are never an ordering key): a strictly
239: later second wins on recency; the same second is a tie that `cmp_window_rank` (8d) decides. The
240: fractional instants stay stored, re-stamped and round-tripped exactly (8i) - bookkeeping, not a
241: key. Within one kind of window (known instants, or legacy aggregates compared at the same
242: granularity) (floor second, rank) is a lexicographic total order. The legacy rule stays - an unknown
243: instant never wins on recency against a known one, the rank alone decides - and to keep the fold
244: order-independent `select_window` keeps the best KNOWN and the best LEGACY candidate per window
245: (`EndpointWindow` slots) and resolves the visible window from that pair (the legacy one only if it
246: outranks the known one by the rank), so the pick is a function of the candidate SET. Inside one
247: second the higher-usage window wins: the conservative side (usage only rises within a window; a
248: reset is already ranked by future/past). Tests: `whole_second_order_is_transitive_for_the_abc_precision_case`
249: (a imprecise :00 50 %, b :00.100 99 %, c :00.900 30 %, six orders -> 99 %),
250: `mixed_precision_candidates_give_one_pick_in_every_order` (six candidates - two imprecise, two with
251: fractions in one second, one in the next second, one legacy, partial windows - 720 orders through
252: the recorded selection and `merge_observation`, plus a recorded/live split); the 8i sub-second test
253: now passes by rank (99 % at :00.900 against live 30 % at :00.100). The plugin's T17 fix uses the
254: same total order.

39: /// Deserialize an optional string so a *present* value (including `null`) becomes `Some(..)`
40: /// and an *absent* key stays `None`: the tri-state `revision_moved` needs (see that field).
41: /// With `#[serde(default)]`, an absent key never calls this and defaults to `None`.
42: fn deserialize_present_string<'de, D>(d: D) -> Result<Option<Option<String>>, D::Error>
43: where
44:     D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,
45: {
46:     Ok(Some(Option::<String>::deserialize(d)?))
47: }

49: /// Same tri-state as [`deserialize_present_string`] for any object record (the wave-26
50: /// `mode_fallback`/`stall`/`tree_check` fields): a *present* value (including `null`) becomes
51: /// `Some(..)`, an *absent* key stays `None` (via `#[serde(default)]`), so a pre-wave-26 store
52: /// round-trips byte-identical while a fresh entry writes the field in position (null or object).
53: fn deserialize_present<'de, D, T>(d: D) -> Result<Option<Option<T>>, D::Error>
54: where
55:     D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,
56:     T: serde::Deserialize<'de>,

58:     Ok(Some(Option::<T>::deserialize(d)?))

{"schema_version":"1","verdict":"ADVISE","verdict_reason":"The proposals are viable, but measurement validity and schema evolution must be settled before committing the closed vocabulary or routing policy.","reply_markdown":"## Framing
The brief combines three separable decisions: selecting effort, measuring it, and routing work. I would separate them behind versioned interfaces. Unlisted options include a randomized safe-band holdout to estimate causal effort effects; active learning that spends high effort only on uncertain cases; a paired replay benchmark over archived diffs with known confirmed findings; and shadow workers whose outputs are scored without influencing the judge. Choosing needs marginal defect recall by purpose, observed cost distributions, latency limits, concurrency on shared accounts, provider capability limits, and the acceptable false-negative rate for acceptance work.

## Q1
Use these defaults, with explicit overrides: **gpt-6-astra** - chore low; checkpoint and reading pass medium; diff-review and framing/decision high; acceptance, core-contract and stuck xhigh. **glm-5.3** - chore and checkpoint low; diff-review, framing and decision high; acceptance high initially; core-contract and stuck max. This is a prior, not a conclusion: medium Astra reading passes and GLM max marginal value require paired trials.

The primary denominator should be confirmed findings per **attributed marginal run cost**, not end-of-run window share. Report three cost dimensions separately: run-attributed 5-hour/weekly window delta or tokens for same-account Astra, monetary cost for cross-provider comparison, and wall time as an SLA constraint. Confirmed findings are the numerator; usefulness is a secondary outcome. A composite may route, but publishing raw numerator and denominators prevents weighting choices from becoming truth. Unlisted design: randomized holdout routing within safe effort bands plus paired replay on archived diffs.

## Q2
SubagentStop is suitable as a terminal signal only when paired with SubagentStart or a coordinator-minted attempt id, so duplicate, missing and resumed stops are detectable. Do not depend on it for effort unless payload tests prove it. Keep prompts, briefs, paths, filenames, repository/task/session/thread/agent identifiers, commands, tool output, user/host names and unlisted model aliases out. Use only closed classes plus a random worker_ref.

Do not assign success directly. Record pseudonymous provenance: attempt_ref, parent_wave_ref, artifact_ref, then later rework_state none|minor|major|replacement and adoption adopted|partial|discarded|unknown. Score completion and rework burden; count confirmed contribution only when the coordinator marks adoption after verification. Other hosts can submit the same event through a CLI-generated manifest, with tier/effort source marked unknown rather than guessed.

## Q3
Add now: schema_version and vocabulary/caps versions; event_kind; consult_ref/worker_ref/attempt_ref/parent_event_id; role scout|judge|direct|worker; purpose/task_class; effort_requested_class, effort_sent, effort_source and mapping_class; tier and tier_source; model_class; host_class; outcome/error/stop classes; duration and token buckets; verification_state; edit_state; adoption/rework classes; rating mark/revision/judge source; routing_mode, input_kind full|digest, scout_ref; call-budget class; attributed token/window/cost/wall-time buckets; confirmed-finding counts and finding-verification version. Every enum needs unknown plus other, and fields must be additive. Versioning matters because a supposedly closed vocabulary still needs semantic revisions.

## Q4
Scout-and-judge fails through false negatives, anchoring on a confident digest, loss of line-level evidence, and a scout selecting the wrong emphasis. Acceptance and core-contract reviews must receive the original diff or path-scoped excerpts; digest-only judging should fail closed. Cap the digest at about 1,500 bytes or 20 claims, each with a path/line locator, evidence status and uncertainty, plus a mandatory unreviewed list. Give the judge at most two clarification calls, but let it request raw excerpts rather than merely more prose.
